title: 4/11–4/12 two scheduler units ran concurrently; every killed orphan was respawned by the other unit
tier_reason: two production schedulers ran on one box with one picks directory and one posting account (duplicate-delivery and state-race hazard), and deploys restarted only one of them, so an old-code scheduler kept running after each deploy; no duplicate post is evidenced

contract.text: Exactly one scheduler runs on the box, as the bts user's systemd unit that each deploy restarts.
contract.source: 8193909 body ('~/.config/systemd/user/bts-scheduler.service … the canonical version'); .github/workflows/deploy.yml user-level restart (cda8c1c)

mechanism.text: the 4/11 01:08 cutover setup installed system-level units (/etc/systemd/system/bts-scheduler.service, Restart=always, RestartSec=300); the canonical user-level units created at 22:04 ran alongside them

the deploy restarted only the user-level units and nothing removed the legacy ones, so each deploy left a second (older-code) scheduler running, and every manual kill was undone by the other unit's restart policy within 5 minutes

residual.text: a second scheduler started any other way is not detected: the deploy self-heal still removes only /etc/systemd/system/bts-{scheduler,dashboard}.service, unit_drift (2026-07-10, audit F12) compares only the installed user units with the repo templates, and no health check counting scheduler processes was found (grep of src/bts/health)

watchdog.trigger: more than one `bts schedule` process (or active scheduler units in both the system and user managers) at any time, or a scheduler process started before the latest successful deploy run
watchdog.recovery_assertion: exactly one scheduler process, from the user-level unit, started after the latest deploy

evidence.what: root cause of the orphan-scheduler-after-every-deploy issue: system-level units (01:08 on 4/11) and user-level units (22:04 on 4/11) ran concurrently, both Restart=always RestartSec=300; 'every "kill orphan" was followed by a fresh orphan from the OTHER unit's restart policy 5 minutes later'
first run with the self-heal step (head 8193909), 2026-04-12T16:37:36Z, concluded success; log expired, so whether the self-heal branch executed is not visible
the deploy restart switched to the bts user's manager, seven minutes after the user-level units were created

notes: link 1 code is empty: the legacy system-level units were box-local (the repo template scripts/bts-scheduler.service had Pi5 paths and Restart=on-failure)
the two-scheduler window overlapped the 4/12 noon lineup checks (I-021, I-022, I-025); no duplicate post is evidenced — the bot's public feed is not an inventoried source
mitigation none: the manual kills were undone by the other unit
